main_body: Two-storey half-timbered house with a large hipped tile roof, a plaster upper wall, a cobblestone ground floor, a wooden door, windows with flower boxes and a hanging sign
top_band: Roof slope of orange and red tiles, rows ~0-43 at x=48. Tile rows alternate light orange L~130-145 with darker maroon L~57-85. A dark eave line sits at rows ~43-45.
evidence: The big tiled hip roof is a clearly visible sloped top surface, with the hip slopes on both sides. It ends in a dark eave line and shadow over the wall. Below it the south wall carries inset windows with sills and flower boxes, a door, and timber framing. This matches the reference houses, whose roof slopes read as top surfaces. It is not a front elevation.

style.evidence: The candidate has 19 colours per tile against 18 and 11 for the references, 191 distinct colours, and 0% flat-fill coverage. Only 12% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines are tinted dark browns and maroons. The roof has per-tile highlights, the plaster is speckled, the cobbles are shaded one by one and the wood has grain. It is at least as rich as the Beodeul references.
